punchline: An ugly lawn billboard went from a hard no to an easy yes because of a tiny window sticker people had agreed to two weeks earlier.
thirty_sec: In a 1966 study described by Robert Cialdini, a volunteer asked homeowners to put a big, unattractive 'Drive Carefully' billboard on their lawn. Only about 17% agreed. But residents who had agreed two weeks earlier to a tiny three-inch safe-driving sign in their window said yes about 76% of the time. The small yes had turned them into civic-minded people in their own eyes, and they acted to stay consistent with that.
question: Would you let a stranger put a huge sign on your lawn, and would your answer change if you'd already agreed to a little one in your window?
